extraction.name: LUMA
extraction.description: A multimodal dataset specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Foumier
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Foumier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Leaming from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th Intemational ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR ’25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were compiled from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset. Audio samples were extracted, validated, and associated from three diverse audio corpora. Text data was generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct LLM.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10 datasets for images; The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice corpora for audio; Gemma-7B Instruct model for text generation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset includes a Python toolkit that allows the injection of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in a controlled and parameterized way, including controlling data diversity, adding real-world noise, randomly switching labels, and injecting out-of-distribution (OOD) data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio samples were automatically validated using OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for transcription. Text samples were validated by masking label occurrences and feeding the text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model for classification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For manual validation of audio samples, annotators were provided the audio sample with a prompt asking if the audio was saying the target word, with 'Yes' or 'No' answer options.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotations achieved a 71.61% agreement rate. Samples were accepted only if both annotators confirmed validity; conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model, Gemma-7B Instruct model
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to help the research community design more trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety-critical applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The generated text modality contains offensive biases and stereotypes, particularly a significant amount of gender bias for the classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl'.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The textual data generated by an LLM may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. The dataset should not be used as a source of knowledge or information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data, including Training and Testing.

name.evidence: We propose LUMA, a unique multimodal dataset, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for leaming from uncertain data.

description.evidence: To address this challenge, we introduce LUMA (Leaming from Uncertain and Multimodal data), a multimodal dataset specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal leaming algorithms on uncertain data. The dataset includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset [ 18], extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora [ 2,15,27], and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct [25] Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset [ 18], extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora [ 2,15,27], and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct [25] Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset [ 18], extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora [ 2,15,27], and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct [25] Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: The provided Python toolkit allows the injection of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in a controlled and parameterized way into each modality specifically... includes various techniques for injecting uncertainty, such as controlling data diversity, adding different types of real-world noise, randomly switching labels to their closest class, and injecting out-of-distribution (OOD) data.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model [ 29] for audio transcription, and transcribed the extracted audio samples. If the transcription corresponded to the class label (or its plural form), then we considered the sample as valid... To validate that the generated texts accurately represent the labels, we masked all label occurrences in the text and fed the masked text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model, asking it to classify the text into one of the labels.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The interface provided the audio sample, with the prompt 'Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra ’s’ or ’es’ in the pronunciation is okay.)' and answer options of 'Yes' or 'No'.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We opted for Label Studio [ 31] to build the labeling interface.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model [ 29] for audio transcription... To validate that the generated texts accurately represent the labels, we masked all label occurrences in the text and fed the masked text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We anticipate that the LUMA dataset will help the research community to design more trustworthy and robust machine leaming approaches for safety critical applications.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: After manually analyzing some of the generated texts, we noticed that there were samples with offensive biases and stereotypes... Particularly, we noticed a lots of gender bias for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy' and 'girl'.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, we recognize that the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies, or biases, but our aim is to offer a benchmark to study uncertainty quantification in multimodal classification settings. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal leaming algorithms on uncertain data... Each generated version of the dataset consists of 600 data records per class (500 for training, and 100 for testing)
